We know that the nerve cell is the structural and functional unit of

Our nervous system consists of more than100 billion of

Dendrites
of one nerve cell connect to the axons of the other nerve cell through

Fig-4: Synapse
Synapse
Synapse is the functional region of contact
between two neurons, where information from one
neuron is transmitted or relayed to another neuron.
Though these are regions of minute gaps and
essentially neurons do not have any protoplasmic
connection between them yet information is passed
from one nerve cell to the other through these gaps
either in the form of chemical or electrical signals
or both.
These synapses are mainly found usually in
the brain, spinal cord and around the spinal cord.
Beyond these areas the axon carries the signals
from brain and spinal cord to respective parts of
our body.

5.4 Pathways: From stimulus to response
In the holding stick activity you observed that there is coordination
between eye and fingers.
Different pathways are taken by nerves to bring
about this coordinated activity.
On the basis of pathways followed, nerves are classified mainly into
three different types.
They are as follows.
(A) Afferent nerves or Sensory nerves :
The nerves which carry messages towards the central nervous system
(spinal cord or brain) from nerve endings on the muscles of different sense
organs are called afferent or sensory nerves.
(B) Efferent nerves or motor nerves :
The nerves which carry messages from the central nervous system to
body parts that shall carry out the response to effector muscles are called
efferent or motor nerves.
(C) Association nerves (Interneurons) :
These nerves link together the afferent and efferent nerves in central
nervous system (brain and spinal cord).

parsed_output.answer: A synapse is the functional region where information is transferred between two neurons. When a stimulus is received by the dendrites of a neuron, it triggers a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse. This impulse travels through the cell body and axon of the neuron. At the synapse, chemicals (neurotransmitters) are released from the end of the axon and cross the gap to reach the next neuron, allowing the transfer of information. This process is essential for communication within the nervous system.
